newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Nine said killed in Pakistan sectarian shooting.
newsitem.headline: Nine said killed in Pakistan sectarian shooting.

text.p: Gunmen sprayed bullets in a bazaar in Pakistan's Punjab province on Monday, killing nine Shi'ite Moslem activists in what seemed to be the latest incident in a wave of sectarian violence, Shi'ite sources in Islamabad said.
There was no immediate police comment about the shooting, which the Shi'ite sources said happened about 11.30 a.m. (0630 GMT) in the southern Punjab town of Shorkot.

They said the gunmen who shot from automatic weapons in the Shorkot bazaar were riding three motorcycles, vehicles usually used in the shootings which the rival Sunni and Shi'ite Moslem militant groups blame on each other's members.

In a separate incident on Monday, a Sunni lawyer, Mian Mohammad Arshad, was killed by gunmen in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore, police said. There were no claims of responsibility for either shooting.

The populous Punjab province has seen a series of tit-for-tat killings between militant groups of the majority Sunni and the minority Shi'ite branches of Islam in which more than 100 people have been killed this year.

On Sunday, a Shi'ite activist, Malik Ghulam Sarwar, was shot by three men on motorcycles as he opened his shop at another Punjab town, Chichawatni, 200 km (125 miles) southwest of Lahore. Sunni groups accuse neighbouring Shi'ite Iran of financing Pakistani Shi'ite militants, while Shi'ites accuse Sunni Saudi Arabia of aiding Sunni groups.
